339342.DESCRIPTION: Calorimetric titrations were performed in a Microcal iTC 200 microcalorimeter. Freshly purified 5 µM protein (Aurora A/B kinases) was titrated against 100 µM ligand (felodipine/ PTK66) in each case at 25 °C. Proteins and the ligandswere diluted in the final dialysate (20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 0.2 mM EDTA and 100 mM KCl) against which the proteins were extensively dialysed to avoid any artefact due to the minor differences in buffer composition. DMSO content was kept exactly same in the cell (not exceeding 0.2% v/v) and syringe to rule out any interference due to DMSO content mismatch. All samples were thoroughly degassed prior to titration and were prepared with the same batch of dialysate to avoid any artefacts from the minor differences in buffer composition. Dilutions of 100 µM felodipine/PTK66 in dialysate containing equal percentage of DMSOserved as controls. The stirring speed was 300 rpm.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: Calorimetric titrations were performed in a Microcal iTC 200 microcalorimeter. Freshly purified 5 µM protein (Aurora A/B kinases) was titrated against 100 µM ligand (felodipine/PTK66) in each case at 25 °C. Proteins and the ligands were diluted in the final dialysate (20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 0.2 mM EDTA and 100 mM KCl) against which the proteins were extensively dialysed to avoid any artefact due to the minor differences in buffer composition. DMSO content was kept exactly same in the cell (not exceeding 0.2% v/v) and syringe to rule out any interference due to DMSO content mismatch. All samples were thoroughly degassed prior to titration and were prepared with the same batch of dialysate to avoid any artefacts from the minor differences in buffer composition. Dilutions of 100 µM felodipine/PTK66 in dialysate containing equal percentage of DMSO served as controls. The stirring speed was 300 rpm. The resulting thermograms (background enthalpy subtracted) were analysed using 'one set of binding sites' model of Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least squares curve fitting algorithm, inbuilt in the MICROCAL LLC software (Northampton, MA, USA).
original_paragraph.Results - Binding sites of PTK66 to Auro: The thermograms and the relevant parameters are shown in Figure S3. Felodipine binds to Aurora A kinase (Figure S2c) but not Aurora B kinase (Figure S2d). By contrast, PTK66 associates with both Aurora A kinase (Figure S2a) and Aurora B kinase (Figure S2b) exhibiting 2:1 binding stoichiometry (ligand: protein) with Aurora A kinase and 1:1 with Aurora B kinase. All the associations are characterised by micromolar dissociation constants. The interactions of Aurora A kinase and Aurora B kinase with PTK66 are enthalpy driven with unfavourable entropy contributions, whereas the association of Aurora A kinase with felodipine is entropy driven at 25 °C with both favourable enthalpy and entropy contributions. Enthalpy–entropy compensation results in comparable free energy changes making ΔG negative and favouring the processes.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2: Surface binding mode of PTK66. (A) Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy spectra of Aurora A kinase (black) and its complex with PTK66 (red) and (B) Aurora B kinase (black) and its complex with PTK66 (red). The spectral accumulation time was 30 second.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3: PTK66 docks favourably with Aurora kinases in silico. (A) Aurora A kinase docked with PTK66 in two binding sites, namely site A and site B. The right panels show the individual close-up snapshots. (B) Aurora B kinase docked with PTK66 along with the close-up snapshot in the right. PTK66 is represented in sticks with carbon, oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen atoms coloured as green, red, blue and white, respectively. The residues in hydrophobic contact and hydrogen bonded are coloured in orange and shown as sticks (right). The hydrogen bond is shown as dotted lines. (C) The binding energy, inhibition constant, total internal energy, electrostatic energy and hydrogen bond forming residues of the docked conformation of PTK66 to Aurora A and B kinases are shown in tabulated form.
